rows.what_the_ink_shows: In the uncancelled N.B. in the left margin, the first equation reads lambda^2=q^i. In the next equation, the equality sign is followed directly by the opening parenthesis of (q^{1/2})^i; there is no intervening plus/minus sign or separate minus stroke. ‘cas trivial’ follows and is underlined (crops/15_scan094_L285_real_note.jpg).
rows.note: Written: lambda=(q^{1/2})^i. Intended mathematical reading: lambda=±(q^{1/2})^i. The missing sign is an author's mathematical omission, not a transcription misreading. Preserve the source equation; record the two-root correction in this note only.

rows.event_outcome: Visually collated the full scan and the enlarged contrast-raised marginal-note crop. Confirmed that the ink has no ± between the equality sign and the opening parenthesis. The transcription therefore stays as written.

additional_events.outcome: For q>0 and integer i, set a=(sqrt(q))^i>0. From lambda^2=q^i=a^2 with real lambda, (lambda-a)(lambda+a)=0, so lambda=a or lambda=-a. This verifies the missing-sign objection independently of the ink reading; for example q=4, i=1, lambda=-2 satisfies the squared equation but not the written positive-root equation.

rows.what_the_ink_shows: The proposition's header visibly says q in Q^{++}; the superscript has two plus marks and is followed by ‘Conditions équivalentes’, with no q!=1 qualification (crops/15_scan094_L286_header.jpg). In (iii), the page shows the j, epsilon sequence, epsilon j(lambda)=lambda^2, the inserted compactness condition on Ker epsilon, and epsilon(f)=q (crops/15_scan094_L286_condition_iii.jpg). There is no written exclusion of q=1 in those places.
rows.note: Written: q in Q^{++}, with the literal conditions epsilon∘j(t)=t^2, compact Ker epsilon, and epsilon(f)=q. The correction row proposes an additional q!=1 hypothesis for (i)=>(iii); that is a mathematical restriction rather than a missing phrase visible in the scan, so preserve the source. A limited check of the literal (iii) shows that no blanket incompatibility of q=1 with epsilon∘j=t^2 follows from that condition: for G=G_m, j=id, epsilon(t)=t^2 and f=1, epsilon is nontrivial although epsilon(f)=1, since evaluation at f need not be injective. This only verifies that (iii) admits q=lambda=1. It does not settle the complete equivalence or all q=1 cases; the general need for extra hypotheses remains mathematically unverified. The ink itself is settled.

rows.event_outcome: Visually collated the whole scan and two enlarged contrast-raised crops. Confirmed the positive-rational hypothesis and the stated epsilon/j conditions without a q!=1 restriction. Recorded the proposed restriction as mathematical commentary, leaving all transcription unchanged.

additional_events.outcome: Checked one explicit instance of the literal displayed condition (iii): over Q take G=G_m, j=id, epsilon(t)=t^2, f=1, q=1, and the standard one-dimensional Q-representation, so lambda=1. Then epsilon∘j(t)=t^2, epsilon(f)=1, Ker epsilon=mu_2 has finite compact real points, and f acts with eigenvalue 1. Evaluation of characters at f is not injective, so epsilon(f)=1 does not force epsilon to be the trivial character. This establishes only that (iii) admits this q=lambda=1 instance and that the asserted blanket incompatibility is not a consequence of literal (iii); it does not prove the full q=1 implication/equivalence or refute the correction row in every possible intended scope.
